candidates.name: HISTORICAL_EXECUTION_SEMANTICS
candidates.alternative_physical_distance_equivalent: If unary is interpreted as true distance in mm, each edge costs 1296 mm after integerization; finite unary saturation is 400000 mm.

candidates.name: DOCUMENTED_COMMON_MM_SEMANTICS
candidates.evidence_scope: Recorded design contract, not a claim of prior explicit Human approval of the fix
candidates.energy: sum_v min(d_label_mm(v),400 mm) + (TAU_mm/3)*number_of_cut_edges; hard pins replace terminal costs
candidates.reason: Published unary is geodesic distance, published pairwise is TAU/3 mm, generated cap metadata is 400 mm. A sum of physical length costs requires common units. Executable ambiguity check and pre-mincut distance probe explicitly convert the same metre geodesic to mm. No 0.001 unary coefficient or metre-cost tradeoff is specified. The missing conversion occurs only in terminal capacity assembly (and duplicated rerun).

candidates.name: DIMENSIONLESS_NORMALIZED_SEMANTICS
candidates.reason: No source declares a common reference length L_ref and a dimensionless smoothness coefficient, nor divides both distance and TAU by that length. No test contract defines normalized rounding.
candidates.mathematical_note: Dividing an already unit-consistent energy by a shared positive length would preserve continuous ordering, but choosing L_ref and integerization now would be a new design. It does not explain the historical asymmetric factor of 1000.

verdict_scope: Finite local tradeoff at 1/5/10/20 mm: one boundary edge costs 1296/259.2/129.6/64.8 times the respective unary. This does not assert the pairwise term dominates every global energy sum or overrules hard pins. The relevant label change is unary DIFFERENCE; absolute example costs supply scale only.
